I was thinking about this while I read your thread. When I was a little kid, I was obsessed with ghosts, ghost stories, things that go bump in the night, etc. I was always sure I could see or talk to them. I remember at some point I tried to ask a ghost who was with me at all times, a little girl whose name I have forgotten, what she was doing in this world with me. She was so sad and confused and lost and she said “I don’t know.”

Eventually I forgot about ghosts and thought I outgrew that silly obsession. But I think it came back as a more sophisticated and less literal one: the idea that the world as I saw it was actually more real and “correct” than it seemed to be, and that what I saw around me was some sort of veneer for a more interesting world.

This is a very popular belief. I’m not saying I’m special or that it’s unique to me. I think a lot of people have this. But I think it’s interesting that you’re talking about a future where things are more transparent, where there are fewer layers of reality, and I think my childhood self would have thought that was awesome! The idea that ghosts were actually real was a lot more terrifying and lonely to me than the idea that the world was more transparent and I could see more.
